title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-02-08

ai_review.summary: Fair matrix recording with a stellar performance – Smokestack Lightning opener, epic Lovelight and multiple standout jams.
ai_review.review: The composite SBD/Audience (matrix) source is decent but shows balance issues, a tinny‑phased texture and low drum levels that keep it from being great. Musically the show shines: the legendary Smokestack Lightning opening, soaring Morning Dew, tight China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, a superb St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > St. Stephen sandwich, an inspired Dark Star, and a marathon Lovelight that many reviewers call one of the best of ’70.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is consistently praised (many 4‑5★ reviews) while recording quality is described as only fair with specific mix problems; weighted average yields ~4.1★.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Composite of soundboard and audience sources; generally clear but drums are low, overall mix is off‑balance, some tinny/phased artifacts and occasional drop‑outs.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > St. Stephen
Sitting On Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows beautifully, opening with a powerful Smokestack Lightning, moving through rare early‑’70 gems and culminating in a 35‑minute Lovelight that many consider a highlight of the era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s interplay with Weir is highlighted; his guitar work on China Cat and throughout the jams receives strong praise.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm/vocal contributions are noted for their chemistry with Garcia, especially in the SBD sections.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten (TC) is mentioned as a filler after leaving the band; keyboards aren’t a focal point but no negative remarks.
band_member_comments.Drums: Multiple reviewers note drum levels are low or slightly buried in the mix.
